title: Participatory Moral AI Is Not Neutral: The Invisible Hand of Developers
abstract: arXiv:2608.14522v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As AI systems make more morally loaded decisions across society, one response has been moral preference elicitation. In this approach, researchers poll participants on hypothetical dilemmas and use the aggregated votes to train a policy that an AI model then applies at scale. Before any vote is cast, developers make three key choices in the moral AI elicitation pipeline: feature scoping, voter sampling, and question framing. In other words, they decide which features go to a vote, which voters to include, and how to present the question. These choices are often opaque, undocumented, and treated as technical details rather than normative ones. We examine each of these choices within a common empirical study and show that each can shape the preferences produced by moral AI elicitation. translated_title: 参与式道德AI并非中立：开发者背后的无形之手
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14522v1 公告类型：新 摘要：随着AI系统在社会中做出更多涉及道德决策的选择，一种应对方式是道德偏好 elicitation。在这种方法中，研究人员就假设性困境向参与者进行调查，并使用汇总的投票结果来训练AI模型随后大规模应用的政策。在投票进行之前，开发者在道德AI elicitation流程中做出三个关键选择：特征范围界定、选民抽样和问题框架。换句话说，他们决定哪些特征需要投票，包括哪些选民，以及如何呈现问题。这些选择往往不透明、未记录，并且被视为技术细节而非规范性内容。我们在一个常见的实证研究中考察了每个选择，并表明每个选择都可能影响道德AI elicitation产生的偏好。在两个阶段（N=809）和三个部署背景（即AI肾脏分配、模拟缺席工人的AI代理和生成式AI描绘）中，我们展示了这些选择如何导致不同结果。
tldr: 本论文揭示道德AI elicitation过程中开发者做出的特征范围、选民抽样和问题框架三个关键选择并非中立，而是显著影响最终道德偏好的产生。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that developers' three key choices in moral AI elicitation—feature scoping, voter sampling, and question framing—are not neutral and significantly shape the resulting moral preferences.
